correctness.rationale: Exactly eight of the 32 binary five-bit words are palindromes, leaving 20 reversal classes, hence no distinct-class circular walk exceeds length 20. In the 16-state order-four de Bruijn graph, a valid circular identifier is exactly a closed walk whose edge reversal-class mask has no repeated bit. The deterministic graph-first recursion tests both extensions at every state and all 16 roots up to depth 20; the proved bijection between closed walks and circular words establishes exhaustiveness. It expands 3242 nodes and yields exactly 20 rotation classes with frequencies 2,4,4,4,2,4 at lengths 6,7,8,9,10,12. A separate enumeration of every indexed binary word at all lengths 5..20 agrees exactly. All within-length pairs of observation masks overlap, proving codebook size at most 1, attained precisely at those six lengths. Scripts, exact census, and instructions are embedded.

value.rationale: The object models a five-symbol circular marker viewed without a trusted reading direction, when only the identity of the observed arc position matters. It is motivated by the difference between orientation-sensitive robot identifiers and reversal-class-based optical reads. The answer is the complete exact possible-circumference set and the entire twenty-word list, plus the sharp maximum possible circumference 12 and the exact codebook capacity for every k>=5. These establish a nontrivial capacity collapse relative to the ordered model and provide a full finite design boundary. The five-symbol read length is the literature’s concrete robot-marking example and not an arbitrary thin slice.
